title: Strongest Bit-Prefix Array
src: Media.net OA, college not given (second set in the same shared note), problem 1. The statement was garbled in the note; the definition below is the one that reproduces both reported examples.
body:
You are given an array A of N integers below 220. Arrange its elements in any order Z (a permutation of A).

The power array X of Z has 20 entries. X[i] is the length of the longest prefix of Z in which every element has bit 19 − i set (so X[0] is about the highest bit, 219, and X[19] about bit 0).

Power arrays are compared lexicographically: F beats G if at the first index where they differ, F is larger. Return the largest power array any arrangement can produce.

Function to complete

Complete bestPowerArray(A). It returns the 20 entries of the largest power array.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
out: The 20 entries of the best power array on one line.

spec.returns: the 20 entries of the largest power array

ref:
class Solution:
    def bestPowerArray(self, A: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        # Keep the arrangement as an ordered list of groups whose inner order is still free.
        # For each bit (highest first) walk the groups: a group whose elements all have the bit
        # extends the prefix; the first group that doesn't is split into (has bit, lacks bit).
        groups = [list(A)]; res = []
        for i in range(20):
            b = 19 - i; x = 0
            for gi, g in enumerate(groups):
                w = [v for v in g if v >> b & 1]
                if len(w) == len(g):
                    x += len(g); continue
                x += len(w)
                if w: groups[gi:gi + 1] = [w, [v for v in g if not v >> b & 1]]
                break
            res.append(x)
        return res

wrong.why: counts the elements with each bit, ignoring that one order must serve every bit

samples.ex: Order 5 4 3 2 1: the prefix 5, 4 has bit 2 set (X[17] = 2); 5 lacks bit 1 (X[18] = 0); 5 has bit 0 but 4 doesn't (X[19] = 1).
Order 36 36 4 16 16: bit 5 holds for 36, 36 (X[14] = 2); bit 4 fails at once (X[15] = 0); bit 2 holds for 36, 36, 4 (X[17] = 3).
